description: Modified-sandwich SettingsModel checkpoint: SerializationTests::ColorScheme, GlobalSettings, Actions, Profile, CascadiaSettings, LegacyFontSettings, ProfileWithInvalidIcon, DontRoundtripNoReloadEnvVars, RoundtripReloadEnvVars, all three color-scheme collision round-trips, RoundtripGenerateActionID, NoGeneratedIDsForIterableAndNestedCommands, GeneratedActionIDsEqualForIdenticalCommands, plus color-scheme/profile/global mutation round-trips are backed by safe Rust owners with Microsoft-derived typed JSON evidence.

entries.notes: Microsoft SerializationTests::ColorScheme uses the same Campbell object as the existing ColorScheme contract: foreground #F2F2F2, background #0C0C0C, cursor #FFFFFF, selection #131313 and all sixteen ANSI table colors. The safe Rust ColorScheme owner parses that exact vector and projects a structure-identical typed JSON value, satisfying the FromJson/ToJson round-trip without introducing a second settings owner.

Microsoft round-trips both the full GlobalAppSettings vector and a minimal defaultProfile/actions/keybindings vector. Safe Rust SettingsDocument retains the shared typed JSON tree as its serialization source of truth; the Microsoft-derived witness uses those exact vectors, verifies structure-identical round-trip, and checks representative numeric, boolean, string, warning and empty-array settings without inventing a parallel serializer.

Microsoft round-trips fifteen ActionMap/GlobalAppSettings vectors covering simple commands, object commands and arguments, keybindings, icons/names, new-terminal args, meaningful null, nested command groups, iterable commands and an unbound keybinding. Safe Rust ActionMapDocument accepts the same bare-array and actions/keybindings object forms, recursively validates portable command/group structure, retains the shared typed JSON tree and the witness requires every Microsoft vector to project structure-identically. Generated-ID and legacy-action fixups are intentionally not claimed here because Microsoft covers them in separate SerializationTests contracts.

Microsoft round-trips six Profile vectors: the full Windows PowerShell profile, a minimal name-only profile, a nullable-color profile, explicit icon, null icon, and icon=none. Safe Rust routes these vectors through the existing Profile semantic owner before retaining the complete shared typed JSON tree, so migrated GUID/color/icon/history/directory/environment semantics are validated while unmigrated members remain lossless without a second profile serializer.

Microsoft SerializationTests::CascadiaSettings round-trips the aggregate settings model rather than one leaf owner. Safe Rust CascadiaSettingsDocument composes the existing SettingsDocument typed tree, validates portable profiles/schemes/actions/keybindings aggregate shapes, and the Microsoft-derived witness proves globals, profile identity/commandline, scheme colors, actions and keybindings survive together without introducing a second serializer.

Microsoft loads a profile using legacy fontFace/fontSize/fontWeight and expects Profile::ToJson to emit only the modern font object with face=Cascadia Mono, size=12 and weight=normal. Safe Rust SettingsDocument now canonicalizes those aliases during profile serialization while retaining the same Profile validation and shared typed tree, and the witness checks both exact structure and removal of all three legacy keys.

Microsoft verifies that an icon path which cannot be resolved at load time is still serialized exactly as the user wrote it, rather than as null or as the commandline fallback. Safe Rust CascadiaSettingsDocument now canonicalizes legacy root profiles arrays into the modern profiles.list shape while retaining the original typed profile fields; the witness uses the exact c:\this_icon_had_better_not_exist.tiff vector and verifies icon, commandline and history remain intact.

Microsoft verifies that settings which never specify compatibility.reloadEnvironmentVariables do not acquire that setting during fixup/round-trip. Safe Rust CascadiaSettingsDocument canonicalizes the legacy profiles array without synthesizing either the legacy root property or a profiles.defaults object; the Microsoft-derived witness uses the exact profile/action vector and verifies unrelated profile and action data remain present.

Microsoft loads legacy settings with root compatibility.reloadEnvironmentVariables=false, runs SettingsLoader fixup, and expects the value to be emitted under profiles.defaults while profiles becomes the modern object/list shape and unrelated actions survive. Safe Rust SettingsDocument now performs that same localized migration during legacy profile canonicalization; the witness uses Microsoft's old/new vectors and requires structure-identical Rust projections.

Microsoft layers a user-modified Campbell over the inbox Campbell plus a user Tango Dark identical to inbox, then FixupUserSettings must preserve the modified Campbell user definition, remove the redundant Tango Dark definition, canonicalize profiles, emit actions=[], and materialize profiles.defaults.colorScheme=Campbell (modified). Safe Rust reuses ColorSchemeSettings::from_layers for collision/reference semantics and SettingsDocument now projects that layered result back to the exact Microsoft user-settings write-back shape; the witness compares Microsoft's complete old/new vectors structurally.

Microsoft layers a user-modified Tango Dark over inbox Tango Dark while no profile references that scheme, then FixupUserSettings must rename only the user definition to Tango Dark (modified), canonicalize profiles, emit actions=[] and avoid materializing profiles.defaults. Safe Rust uses the same ColorSchemeSettings collision owner, deterministically reproduces its modified-name allocation, checks whether the generated target is effectively referenced, and renames only unreferenced modified collisions in the serialized user tree. The witness compares Microsoft's complete old/new vectors structurally and verifies all #111111 colors survive unchanged.

Microsoft layers a user Tango Dark definition that is merge-equivalent to the inbox Tango Dark and expects FixupUserSettings to delete the redundant user copy, canonicalize profiles, emit actions=[] and serialize schemes=[]. The existing safe Rust SettingsDocument collision write-back already removes semantically redundant user schemes using the same foreground/background/16-color-table merge fingerprint; the direct witness uses Microsoft's complete old/new vectors and additionally verifies no profiles.defaults is synthesized.

Microsoft loads a legacy sendInput action without an explicit ID, resolves it through the ctrl+shift+w key chord and expects ActionAndArgs::GenerateID to produce User.sendInput.<hash>. Safe Rust ActionMapDocument now resolves legacy keys-inside-action bindings and reproduces Microsoft's TIL hash over UTF-16 sendInput arguments, including the architecture-specific 32-bit 56911147 and 64-bit A020D2 vectors, instead of hardcoding the observed ID.

Microsoft expects SettingsLoader/ActionMap to report no user-settings fixup for three shapes: an ordinary action with an explicit ID and no legacy keys, an iterable command, and a nested command group. Safe Rust ActionMapDocument now mirrors ActionMap::LayerJson's user-origin fixup predicate: ordinary commands request write-back only when the ID is absent or legacy inline keys are present; iterable and nested groups are excluded. The direct witness uses Microsoft's exact three-entry vector and also exercises both positive branches of the native predicate.

Microsoft loads two separate settings documents containing the same legacy sendInput action (same name, input and ctrl+shift+w key chord) and intends the generated action IDs to compare equal. Safe Rust ActionMapDocument derives the ID solely from the command semantics using the Microsoft-compatible generated-ID hash owner, so the direct witness resolves both exact source vectors independently, requires both documents to request fixup, requires both key chords to resolve, and proves the resulting User.sendInput.* IDs are identical.

Microsoft loads a settings document containing user scheme MyScheme, changes foreground from #CCCCCC to #AABBCC and verifies ToJson persists that mutation while retaining the scheme. Safe Rust SettingsDocument owns the typed settings tree, performs that exact named-scheme mutation, and the Microsoft-derived witness additionally verifies unrelated defaultProfile/profiles and background survive unchanged.

Microsoft mutates profile zero historySize from 1000 to 5000, verifies commandline cmd.exe survives, then adds tabTitle NewTitle and verifies ToJson. Safe Rust SettingsDocument performs those exact typed mutations over the retained settings tree for both legacy profiles arrays and modern profiles.list shape.

Microsoft loads initialRows=30 and alwaysOnTop=false, mutates them through the global settings owner to 50 and true, then verifies serialization reflects both changes. Safe Rust SettingsDocument performs those exact typed root mutations while retaining defaultProfile and profiles unchanged.
